title: Article from 6/18
text:
The proliferation of direct-to-consumer genetic testing services has democratised access to genomic information while simultaneously generating profound ethical dilemmas regarding the governance of this uniquely sensitive category of personal data. By the close of 2024, more than 30 million individuals worldwide had submitted DNA samples to commercial testing platforms, often providing irrevocable consent through user agreements whose implications extend far beyond the immediate consumer transaction. Genetic data, unlike most categories of personal information, simultaneously identifies the individual from whom it derives and reveals probabilistic information about biological relatives who never provided consent—a structural feature that confounds conventional frameworks of individual privacy rights.

Law enforcement applications of consumer genetic databases have generated particular controversy. Investigators have increasingly leveraged genealogical databases to identify suspects in cold-case investigations through partial DNA matches with distant relatives, a technique that resolved several high-profile homicide cases between 2018 and 2023. Yet civil liberties advocates contend that such practices effectively conscript millions of unwitting individuals into a forensic database without explicit authorisation. A 2023 analysis published in Science estimated that approximately 60 per cent of Americans of European descent could be identified through third-cousin matches in existing commercial databases, even if they had never personally submitted genetic material—a finding that fundamentally challenges traditional conceptions of informed consent.

The insurance and employment dimensions of genetic data governance raise equally consequential concerns. While the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act of 2008 prohibits health insurers and employers in the United States from discriminating based on genetic information, this legislation contains significant gaps—life insurance, disability insurance, and long-term care insurance remain entirely unregulated, creating economic incentives for insurers to incorporate genetic risk profiles into underwriting decisions. Researchers suggest that as predictive genetic technologies advance, individuals identified as harbouring elevated risks for late-onset conditions such as Alzheimer's disease or Huntington's disease may face systematic exclusion from financial protection mechanisms, potentially creating what some scholars term genetic underclasses.

International harmonisation of genetic privacy frameworks remains elusive despite repeated calls for coordinated action. Jurisdictions differ substantially in their treatment of genetic information: the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation classifies genetic data as a special category requiring heightened protections, whereas regulatory approaches in many Asian and Latin American jurisdictions remain underdeveloped. This regulatory fragmentation creates opportunities for regulatory arbitrage, whereby commercial operators relocate data processing activities to jurisdictions offering minimal oversight. Experts emphasise that the irreversibility of genetic disclosure—once exposed, an individual's genetic profile cannot be recalled or reset like a compromised password—demands particularly robust safeguards. Whether the international community can establish effective governance before genetic surveillance becomes embedded in routine commercial and governmental practices remains an open question of considerable urgency.

options: easily withdrawn or cancelled
incapable of being undone or recalled
automatically renewed each year
limited to specific medical conditions

explanation.A: 错误。irrevocable 与 easily withdrawn 含义相反，前者强调不可撤销。
explanation.B: 正确。irrevocable 意为不可撤销的、不可挽回的，文中指消费者通过用户协议给出的同意一旦提供便无法收回。
explanation.C: 错误。automatically renewed 与 irrevocable 的含义无关。
explanation.D: 错误。irrevocable 描述同意的性质，与医疗条件无关。

questions.stem: 2. According to Paragraph 2, what did the 2023 Science analysis estimate?
options: Only 6 per cent of Americans could be identified through commercial databases.
Approximately 60 per cent of European-descended Americans could be identified through third-cousin matches.
All Americans had personally submitted DNA to commercial databases.
Genealogical databases failed to resolve any cold-case homicides.

explanation.A: 错误。原文数字是 60% 而非 6%，且对象是 European-descended Americans。
explanation.B: 正确。原文明确指出 approximately 60 per cent of Americans of European descent could be identified through third-cousin matches in existing commercial databases。
explanation.C: 错误。原文说他们 even if they had never personally submitted genetic material 仍可被识别，并非全部都提交过。
explanation.D: 错误。原文指出此技术 resolved several high-profile homicide cases，并非未解决任何案件。

questions.stem: 3. What can be inferred about the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act of 2008?
options: It comprehensively protects against all forms of genetic discrimination.
It applies to all types of insurance including life and disability insurance.
It contains gaps that leave certain insurance categories unregulated.
It has been replaced by more recent legislation in the United States.

explanation.A: 错误。原文明确指出 this legislation contains significant gaps，并非全面保护。
explanation.B: 错误。原文说 life insurance, disability insurance, and long-term care insurance remain entirely unregulated，与该选项相反。
explanation.C: 正确。文中指出该法案包含显著漏洞，特别是 life insurance、disability insurance 和 long-term care insurance 不在监管范围内。
explanation.D: 错误。文中未提及该法案被新立法取代。

questions.stem: 4. The author mentions Alzheimer's disease and Huntington's disease (Paragraph 3) in order to ________.
options: argue that all genetic testing should be banned immediately
illustrate potential late-onset conditions that may lead to insurance exclusion
prove that these diseases have no genetic component
show that current insurance practices are entirely fair

explanation.A: 错误。原文未主张全面禁止基因检测，仅讨论监管缺陷。
explanation.B: 正确。引用这两种疾病作为晚发性疾病的例子，说明遗传风险信息可能导致保险系统性排斥，形成所谓 genetic underclasses。
explanation.C: 错误。这两种疾病恰恰是有明确遗传成分的疾病，原文以此为例。
explanation.D: 错误。原文批评现有保险实践存在系统性问题，而非肯定其公平性。

questions.stem: 5. Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: Genetic Privacy: Governance Challenges in the Age of Consumer DNA Testing
Why Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Testing Should Be Universally Banned
The Complete Success of International Genetic Data Regulation
How Law Enforcement Has Eliminated All Cold-Case Homicides

explanation.A: 正确。全文围绕消费者基因检测时代的隐私治理挑战展开，从不可逆同意、执法应用、保险歧视到国际监管碎片化系统论述。
explanation.B: 错误。文章未主张全面禁止基因检测，而是讨论治理框架。
explanation.C: 错误。原文明确指出 international harmonisation remains elusive，监管远未成功。
explanation.D: 错误。原文只提到 several high-profile cases 被破，并非消除所有冷案。

words.def: 难以捉摸的，难以实现的
